title: Given a string, find the length of its longest palindromic substring, where a substring must be contiguous. Explain the Palindromic Subsequence DP pattern applied to contiguous ranges, the recurrence, the complexity, and a banking use case.
shortTitle: Longest Palindromic Substring (Longest Contiguous Run That Reads the Same Both Ways)

s1_definition.profdef: The Longest Palindromic Substring is the contiguous variant of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern. A range is a palindrome when its two ends match and the inner range is also a palindrome, so we track a boolean table of which ranges are palindromes and keep the longest true range. This gives a quadratic time and space dynamic program.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India scans account statement memo fields and wants the longest unbroken run of characters that reads the same both ways, because such runs are flagged as suspicious auto-generated noise. Unlike the subsequence version, here the characters must sit next to each other with no gaps.
s1_definition.oneliner: A contiguous range is a palindrome when its ends match and the strictly inner range is already a palindrome.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The Longest Palindromic Substring is the contiguous variant of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern. A range is a palindrome when its two ends match and the inner range is also a palindrome, so we track a boolean table of which ranges are palindromes and keep the longest true range. This gives a quadratic time and space dynamic program.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** The National Bank of India scans account statement memo fields and wants the longest unbroken run of characters that reads the same both ways, because such runs are flagged as suspicious auto-generated noise. Unlike the subsequence version, here the characters must sit next to each other with no gaps.

**One line to remember:** A contiguous range is a palindrome when its ends match and the strictly inner range is already a palindrome.

sections.s2_technical:
We keep a boolean table where the entry for a range i to j is true when the substring from i to j is a palindrome. The recurrence is that a range is a palindrome when the character at i equals the character at j and either the range has length at most two or the strictly inner range i plus one to j minus one is also a palindrome. We fill by increasing length and remember the start and length of the longest true range.

Bottom-up: `for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { dp[i][i] = true; for (int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) { if (s.charAt(i) == s.charAt(j) && (j - i < 2 || dp[i+1][j-1])) { dp[i][j] = true; if (j - i + 1 > bestLen) { bestLen = j - i + 1; } } } }`. A concrete check: for a memo containing an embedded symmetric run, the longest true range matches that run exactly. Senior nuance: this is quadratic in time and space, the expand-around-center method also solves it in quadratic time with constant space, and Manacher's algorithm reaches linear time but is rarely needed in practice.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India scans the memo field on statements for the longest unbroken run of characters that reads the same forward and backward, because long symmetric runs are a signature of auto-generated spam memos that the fraud team wants flagged. Checking every substring naively is cubic. This is exactly how the Longest Palindromic Substring works: it finds the longest contiguous palindrome in quadratic time with the ends-match-and-inner-is-palindrome recurrence.

The code defines a `MemoScanService` exposing `longestSymmetricRun(memo)` returning the length of the longest palindromic substring. A `Demo` runs it over a sample memo and logs the length.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is the memo PAYLEVELHJ. We want the longest contiguous run that reads the same both ways.

Step 1 — We seed the diagonal: every single character is a palindrome of length one, so the best so far is one.

Step 2 — We check adjacent pairs. None of PA, AY, YL and so on have equal neighbours, so no pair of length two becomes true here.

Step 3 — We check length three ranges. The range LEV has ends L and V which differ, but the range EVE has ends E and E that match with a single inner character, so EVE becomes true and the best length rises to three.

Step 4 — We check length five ranges. The range LEVEL has ends L and L that match, and its inner range EVE is already true, so LEVEL becomes true and the best length rises to five.

Step 5 — No longer range qualifies, so the answer is five, the length of LEVEL. The output is below.

```
Oct 27, 2026 9:07:02 PM com.bank.memo.service.MemoScanService longestSymmetricRun
INFO: Longest symmetric run in memo = 5
Oct 27, 2026 9:07:02 PM com.bank.memo.MemoScanApplication main
INFO: Longest symmetric memo run length is 5
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Input: memo = "PAYLEVELHJ"
    │
    ▼
  seed diagonal: every char = palindrome len 1
    │ len 2: ends match? none here
    │ len 3: EVE → E==E, inner single → true (best=3)
    │ len 5: LEVEL → L==L, inner EVE true → true (best=5)
    ▼
  Output: longest symmetric run = 5
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
The Longest Palindromic Substring is the contiguous member of the Palindromic Subsequence pattern family, and the recurrence I rely on is that a contiguous range is a palindrome exactly when its two end characters are equal and the strictly inner range is itself a palindrome, with ranges of length one or two handled as simple base cases. I keep a boolean table marking which ranges are palindromes and track the start and length of the longest range that comes out true.

I fill the table by increasing range length so that the inner range is always decided before the outer range that depends on it, which runs in quadratic time and space. I usually mention that expand-around-center achieves the same quadratic time with constant extra space, and that Manacher's algorithm reaches linear time, though I rarely need it. The crucial point I make is that this version demands adjacency, which is what separates it from the subsequence version that allows gaps.

At the National Bank of India I used this to scan statement memo fields for the longest unbroken symmetric run, because the fraud team treated long symmetric runs as a signature of auto-generated spam memos worth flagging. I ran the contiguous range dynamic program over each memo and returned the longest run length. Describing the ends-match-and-inner-palindrome recurrence, the length-ordered fill, and the contrast with the subsequence version is what tells an interviewer I truly understand the Palindromic Subsequence pattern as applied to contiguous substrings.
